subject: Biology
topic: Plant Reproduction — pollination, double fertilization, seed dispersal, apomixis
description: Sexual reproduction in plants: types of pollination (agents), double fertilization (unique to angiosperms), seed dispersal mechanisms, apomixis, cleistogamy, polyembryony — IBPS PO/SSC CGL/UPSC standard.

questions.stem: Double fertilization, a unique feature of angiosperms, results in:

options.option_text: Formation of diploid (2n) embryo AND triploid (3n) endosperm from two sperm nuclei
Formation of two separate embryos in the same ovule — hence the term double fertilization
Fertilization occurring twice in a season — once in spring and once in autumn
Fusion of two egg cells by a single sperm cell — producing one embryo with doubled genetic material

questions.explanation: DOUBLE FERTILIZATION (discovered by Nawaschin, 1898): unique to ANGIOSPERMS (flowering plants). PROCESS: a pollen grain produces TWO sperm nuclei. (1) FIRST FERTILIZATION: one sperm (n) + egg cell (n) → ZYGOTE (2n) → embryo. (2) SECOND FERTILIZATION: other sperm (n) + two polar nuclei (n + n) → PRIMARY ENDOSPERM NUCLEUS (3n) → endosperm (nutritive tissue). ENDOSPERM: stores food (starch, proteins, oils) to nourish the growing seedling. Examples of endosperm food: coconut milk, wheat grain, corn kernel. GYMNOSPERMS: have simple fertilization (no double fertilization, no endosperm in the angiosperm sense). SIGNIFICANCE OF DOUBLE FERTILIZATION: both embryo AND food reserve are produced simultaneously from the same fertilization event — highly efficient. POLYGONUM TYPE: the most common embryo sac (8-nucleate: 1 egg, 2 synergids, 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei, 3 antipodals). PYQ FREQUENCY: double fertilization in SSC CGL, IBPS PO Biology GA, UPSC Prelims GS-3 — 1-2× per cycle.

options.option_text: Wind — pollen is light, dry, and produced in large quantities for wind dispersal
Water — water-mediated pollination is called hydrophily, not anemophily
Insects — insect-mediated pollination is called entomophily, not anemophily
Birds — bird-mediated pollination is called ornithophily, not anemophily

questions.explanation: POLLINATION AGENTS AND GREEK NAMES: (1) ANEMOPHILY = WIND (Greek 'anemos' = wind). Examples: corn/maize, grasses, wheat, coconut palm, date palm. FEATURES: light, dry, dusty pollen; feathery stigmas to trap pollen; no nectar/fragrance; small flowers. Causes hay fever (allergic rhinitis). (2) ENTOMOPHILY = INSECTS (Greek 'entomon' = insect). Most common — bees, butterflies, moths. Colourful, fragrant flowers with nectar. (3) ORNITHOPHILY = BIRDS (Greek 'ornis' = bird). Hummingbirds, sunbirds. Tubular red/orange flowers (no UV pattern needed — birds see no UV). (4) HYDROPHILY = WATER. Hydrilla, Vallisneria (submerged aquatics). CHIROPTEROPHILY = bats (nocturnal, large flowers). MALACOPHILY = snails. EXAM NICHE: 'anemophily causes pollen allergy' — sometimes tested in environmental health context. PYQ FREQUENCY: anemophily in SSC CGL, IBPS PO Biology GA, RRB NTPC — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Cleistogamy, observed in plants like Commelina and Viola, is the phenomenon where:

options.option_text: Flowers never open — pollination and fertilization occur within the closed bud (obligate self-pollination)
Flowers open only at night — nocturnal blooming adapted for bat or moth pollination
Pollen is enclosed inside a capsule and only released when insects break it open mechanically
Seeds are retained inside the fruit indefinitely until the fruit rots on the parent plant

questions.explanation: CLEISTOGAMY = KLEISTOS (closed) + GAMOS (marriage) = fertilization within a closed flower. SIGNIFICANCE: guarantees seed set even when pollinators are absent (drought, winter, darkness). EXAMPLES: Viola (violets) — produce closed cleistogamous flowers along with open chasmogamous ones. Commelina — commonly seen in Indian gardens. Oxalis — also cleistogamous. ADVANTAGE: assured reproduction, less energy expenditure (no nectar, no bright colours needed). DISADVANTAGE: no genetic variation (complete self-pollination = inbreeding). CHASMOGAMY vs CLEISTOGAMY: Chasmogamy = open flowers (cross-pollination possible). Cleistogamy = closed flowers (only self-pollination). OPPOSITE of cleistogamy in terms of mechanism: DICHOGAMY (anther maturation at different times from stigma) prevents self-pollination. AUTOGAMY vs CLEISTOGAMY: autogamy can occur in open or closed flowers; cleistogamy is specifically the closed-flower type. PYQ FREQUENCY: cleistogamy in UPSC Prelims Biology, SSC CGL, IBPS PO — 1× per 2-3 years.

questions.stem: Coconut seeds are dispersed by water (hydrochory). The structural adaptation that enables this is:

options.option_text: A thick fibrous husk (mesocarp) with air-filled fibres that provide buoyancy for float-dispersal
A sticky outer coating that helps the seed attach to the feathers of seabirds for long-distance transport
A parachute-like pappus similar to dandelion that allows the seed to fly over water bodies
An explosive seed pod that catapults the seed into water bodies located nearby

questions.explanation: COCONUT (Cocos nucifera) HYDROCHORY: the coconut fruit has three layers: (1) outer smooth EPICARP (exocarp). (2) thick fibrous MESOCARP (husk — the coir fibres) — contains air pockets that make the fruit BUOYANT. (3) hard inner ENDOCARP (shell) — protects the seed. The fibrous mesocarp allows coconuts to float on seawater for months and remain viable. DISPERSAL MECHANISM TABLE: (a) WIND (anemochory): dandelion (pappus/parachute), maple (winged samaras), cotton (fluffy fibres), Calotropis. (b) WATER (hydrochory): coconut, lotus (hollow thalamus), water hyacinth, mangroves. (c) ANIMALS — external (epizoochory): Xanthium (hooks), Urena (velcro-like), Tribulus. (d) ANIMALS — internal (endozoochory): fruits eaten, seeds pass through gut — tomato, guava, berries. (e) EXPLOSIVE (autochory): Impatiens/touch-me-not, squirting cucumber, Balsam. PYQ FREQUENCY: coconut dispersal mechanism in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, UPSC Prelims Biology — 1× per 2-3 years.

options.option_text: Seed production without fertilization — the embryo develops from an unfertilized egg or maternal tissue
Vegetative reproduction exclusively by underground stems such as rhizomes, corms, and stolons
Fusion of genetically identical gametes within the same plant — a form of forced self-fertilization
Cross-pollination between genetically dissimilar plants — maximising genetic diversity in offspring

questions.explanation: APOMIXIS = APO (without) + MIXIS (mixing/fertilization) = seed formation WITHOUT fertilization. The embryo may arise from: (1) DIPLOSPORY: unreduced egg cell (2n) develops into embryo without fertilization. (2) APOSPORY: somatic cell of the ovule develops into an embryo sac, then embryo. (3) ADVENTIVE EMBRYONY (nucellar polyembryony): cells of the nucellus develop into embryos — common in Citrus, mango. COMMERCIAL SIGNIFICANCE: seedlings from apomictic seeds are genetically IDENTICAL to the parent (no genetic variation) — reliable for fruit production. Citrus rootstocks are often apomictic (nucellar seedlings). HYBRID SEED TECHNOLOGY: if crops are made apomictic, hybrid vigour can be preserved across generations — currently a major agricultural goal (currently hybrids are re-made each generation as seeds don't breed true). POLYEMBRYONY: presence of multiple embryos in a single seed — often involves apomixis. PYQ FREQUENCY: apomixis definition in UPSC Prelims Biology, IBPS PO — 1× per 2-3 years.

questions.stem: Pollen tube growth through the style toward the ovule is guided by a process called:

options.option_text: Chemotropism — the tube is attracted by calcium gradients and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) from the ovule
Phototropism — the tube follows the light gradient from the style down to the ovule
Geotropism — gravity pulls the pollen tube directly downward through the style to the ovule
Thigmotropism — physical contact with stylar cells directs the tube mechanically to the ovule

questions.explanation: POLLEN TUBE GUIDANCE: after a pollen grain germinates on the stigma, the pollen tube grows through the style toward the ovule — guided by CHEMOTROPISM (chemical signals from the ovule). CHEMICAL SIGNALS: (1) CALCIUM GRADIENT: Ca²⁺ concentration increases toward the micropyle — pollen tube grows toward higher Ca²⁺. (2) GAMMA-AMINOBUTYRIC ACID (GABA): secreted by synergid cells near the ovule — attracts pollen tube. (3) Defensin-like proteins (lures) secreted by synergids. SYNERGIDS: two cells flanking the egg cell — they guide and attract the pollen tube. AFTER ENTRY: pollen tube enters through the MICROPYLE (usually) → discharges two sperm cells into the synergid → double fertilization. PHOTOTROPISM: toward light — irrelevant inside a style (dark). GEOTROPISM: gravity — style is not always vertical. THIGMOTROPISM: touch response — not the primary guidance mechanism. PYQ FREQUENCY: chemotropism of pollen tube in UPSC Prelims, CBSE XII Biology, IBPS PO — 1× per 2-3 years.

questions.stem: Self-incompatibility in flowering plants is an important mechanism to:

options.option_text: Prevent self-fertilization — the plant recognises its own pollen and rejects it to promote outbreeding
Prevent fertilization altogether — incompatible plants become sterile and rely on vegetative reproduction
Attract only specific pollinators — incompatibility signals guide particular insects to specific flowers
Delay seed germination — seeds become incompatible with their own germination environment

questions.explanation: SELF-INCOMPATIBILITY (SI): a genetic mechanism preventing self-pollination and fertilization. The plant's STIGMA recognises pollen carrying the same S-allele (Self-incompatibility locus) as itself → REJECTS it (pollen tube growth is stopped or the pollen is destroyed). RESULT: promotes CROSS-POLLINATION (outcrossing) → greater genetic diversity. TWO SYSTEMS: (1) GAMETOPHYTIC SI (GSI): pollen tube rejection in the style based on the haploid pollen's S-allele (e.g., Petunia, Nicotiana, Solanum). (2) SPOROPHYTIC SI (SSI): rejection on the stigma surface based on diploid pollen-parent's S-alleles (e.g., Brassica — cabbage, mustard). AGRICULTURAL IMPORTANCE: SI is exploited in hybrid seed production — SI parents crossed to produce F1 hybrids without needing emasculation (removing anthers). Also a problem in crops where you WANT self-pollination (auto-pollination). UPSC ANGLE: heterosis (hybrid vigour) in agriculture; India's hybrid crop programmes (hybrid rice, maize). PYQ FREQUENCY: self-incompatibility mechanism in UPSC GS-3, CBSE XII Biology — 1× per 2-3 years.
